key_insight: A thermodynamically consistent phase-field model couples donor–acceptor phase separation, solvent evaporation, and fluid flow during organic solar-cell active-layer formation.
engineering_relevance: The framework could support simulations linking drying and fluid motion to active-layer morphology in organic photovoltaic manufacturing.
method: Couple incompressible Navier–Stokes, multispecies Cahn–Hilliard, and Allen–Cahn equations.
Include degenerate mobility and cross-diffusion terms.
Prove global-in-time weak-solution existence and total-energy dissipation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports mathematical existence and energy-dissipation results without size constraints on the data, but no experimental validation or numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: Degenerate mobility requires a specialized variational definition of diffusion fluxes, which may complicate numerical implementation.
paper_title: Modeling and analysis of a phase-field model for organic solar cells
